reviewCadence: Reviewed at every phase gate and whenever a new provider, model or external API is introduced.

risks.title: Model isolation violation: Gemini 3.8 Flash reaches dispatch
risks.description: google/antigravity-gemini-3.8-flash (and any gemini-3.8-flash alias) is prohibited from orchestrator, subagent and backup selection. A stale configuration, typo or alias could silently route work to it and invalidate the model-isolation guarantee.
triggers: A provider config reintroduces the model under a new slug.
An agent assignment or fallback names a denied alias.
A new inventory snapshot lists a renamed Gemini 3.8 Flash endpoint.
mitigation: exclusion-policy.json is the authoritative deny list and records the model as unavailable, not merely disfavored.
Every dispatch is validated against the case-insensitive regex gemini[-_. ]?3[._-]?8[-_. ]?flash before the provider call.
resource-assignments.json carries a per-task policyCheck and all assigned models come from the 89 eligible pairs.
The orchestrator itself runs on evren/deepseek-v4.1-flash, so no workflow depends on the excluded model.
risks.contingency: Hard-block the task, record a blocker in execution/blockers.json, reassign to an approved backup model and report the violation as a release blocker.

controls.verification: excludedModelIds contains google/antigravity-gemini-3.8-flash
denyModelIdRegex is case-insensitive and applied before selection
No assignment matches the deny regex; eligibleInventoryModel is true for every task

risks.title: AniList rate limiting or outage degrades adaptation discovery
risks.description: AniList enforces request budgets and returns 429/5xx under bursts. Unthrottled adaptation lookups would slow detail screens, exhaust the quota and leave anime shelves empty.
triggers: HTTP 429 or repeated 5xx from AniList.
Batch size or request rate above the configured budget.
Cold cache after install or data clear.
mitigation: WA-002 builds a single throttled AniList client; no feature calls the API directly.
Requests use batching plus ETag/Last-Modified caching so unchanged titles cost no quota.
429 and 5xx responses use bounded exponential backoff with jitter and a circuit breaker.
Adaptation fetches are asynchronous and never block series detail or the reader.
The cache is persisted so repeated visits do not re-query.
risks.contingency: Serve last-known-good cached adaptations and show a non-blocking degraded notice; continue without adaptation data rather than failing the screen.

controls.verification: Acceptance requires throttle, ETag/batch cache and 429/5xx backoff
Offline fallback test exercises cache miss and provider outage

risks.title: Offline use breaks catalog, adaptations or reader entry
risks.description: Mobile readers lose connectivity. A cold start without network, an unreachable AniList or an absent Kdrama provider must not crash, hang or show an empty library.
triggers: Airplane mode or network loss during navigation.
Provider timeout while loading a shelf or detail screen.
Fresh install with no cached adaptation snapshot.
mitigation: Local catalog remains the source of truth for library, history and downloads.
WA-006 persists a last-known-good adaptation snapshot and renders it with a degraded-mode banner.
WA-005 treats an absent Kdrama provider as a normal empty state, not an error.
MT-003 runs an explicit offline drill before release.
Empty, loading and error states are defined for every new shelf.
risks.contingency: Fall back to cached data, disable network-only actions with an explanation, and let the user retry without leaving the screen.

controls.verification: Offline snapshot and fallback UX are acceptance criteria
Offline and fallback drill is a release gate

risks.title: Content classifier false negative exposes EXPLICIT titles publicly
risks.description: A missed EXPLICIT classification, compound tag or misleading title (for example a party-themed title with adult tags) could surface adult content in the public feed or locked-Vault counts.
triggers: New tag vocabulary or provider metadata shape.
Adversarial title that hides an adult tag.
Classifier rule change without corpus re-run.
mitigation: VC-002 hardens deterministic rules across title, tags, publication type and external ratings.
VC-003 adds false-positive and false-negative fixtures, including the MILF-party trap and compound tags.
VC-004 guarantees EXPLICIT rows are excluded from public paging sources and migrated only into the private realm.
VC-005 verifies locked-Vault emptiness, chip filtering and public-feed exclusion.
risks.contingency: Quarantine ambiguous rows, block the release gate, and add the failing sample to the corpus before re-running migration.

controls.verification: Rule hardening is complete only with corpus evidence
Adversarial corpus passes 100%
Public-feed and locked-Vault isolation tests pass

risks.title: Private realm leakage through storage, cache or screenshots
risks.description: Vault 2.0 splits public and private realms. A shared DAO, paging source, saved-state bundle or missing FLAG_SECURE could hydrate private titles into public UI or expose them in recents.
triggers: A public query joins a private table.
Private navigation state written to saved instance state.
Screenshot or recents preview captures private content.
mitigation: VR-001 defines hard type and query boundaries between realms.
VR-002 separates DAOs, paging sources, caches and session state per realm.
VR-003 adds system credential verification, background lock, panic action and FLAG_SECURE.
VR-005 runs adversarial isolation tests including search, chips and cross-realm joins.
risks.contingency: Treat any leakage as a release blocker, purge affected caches and re-run the full isolation suite.

controls.verification: No shared pager or DAO between realms
FLAG_SECURE and panic behavior verified on device
Dual-realm security and isolation verification passes

risks.title: Physical-device installation remains blocked
risks.description: The Mi 10T (M2007J3SY, Android 12 / API 31) rejects sideloading with INSTALL_FAILED_USER_RESTRICTED. The 10-minute mobile test cannot start until the owner approves installation on the phone.
triggers: Install prompt canceled on the device.
USB installation disabled in developer options.
mitigation: Build and static verification proceed without the device.
Installation steps and evidence requirements are prepared in advance.
No security setting is bypassed or changed by automation.
risks.contingency: Run MT-002 and MT-003 immediately after the owner approves the install; delay the phase gate rather than claim an untested release.

controls.verification: Install exit code and post-install package query are recorded
Blocker closes only after launch is verified

risks.title: Model availability or naming drifts from the dated inventory
risks.description: The 90-model inventory is dated 2026-10-20. Endpoints may be renamed, retired or newly gated, and a dispatched backup identifier may not exist in the current catalog.
triggers: HTTP 404/410 or model-not-found from a provider.
New catalog export differs from providers.json.
A backup model fails to resolve.
mitigation: Every assignment carries 1-2 backup models from distinct providers.
Dispatch performs an allowlist check against the registry before calling the provider.
A failed provider triggers reassignment, never a switch to a prohibited model.
Inventory refresh is a repeatable script (model-registry/refresh-inventory.py).
risks.contingency: Pause the task, record the drift in blockers.json, refresh the snapshot and re-plan affected assignments.

controls.verification: Snapshot retains the source hash and report date
Backups are eligible and provider-diverse

risks.title: Cost or quota overrun because pricing is unknown
risks.description: No provider publishes rates in the inventory. Unmeasured spend could exhaust a plan or trigger paid overflow without approval.
triggers: A provider starts billing or changes plan terms.
A task exhausts context repeatedly.
Paid overflow is proposed.
mitigation: pricing.json and credits.json store null instead of guessed values.
Each task records token usage when available; unknown cost stays null.
Paid overflow requires owner approval before dispatch.
Cheap or flat-rate eligible endpoints are preferred where quality is sufficient.
risks.contingency: Stop dispatch, report measured usage and request a budget decision from the owner.

controls.verification: No fabricated rate is present
Unmeasured tasks are counted explicitly

risks.title: Kdrama metadata provider is unavailable or unstable
risks.description: There is no single canonical Kdrama metadata source equivalent to AniList. A provider may be missing, change shape or require attribution that the UI does not yet show.
triggers: Provider returns empty or schema-invalid payloads.
Attribution requirement changes.
Provider disappears from the configured list.
mitigation: WA-005 defines a pluggable adapter boundary with attribution support.
Provider absence renders a graceful empty state rather than an error.
Cached metadata serves repeat visits.
risks.contingency: Disable the Kdrama shelf entry for the affected build and record the gap; do not block anime or manga features.

controls.verification: Adapter boundary and attribution are acceptance criteria

risks.title: Schedule compression on the critical path
risks.description: PHASE-2 through PHASE-6 total roughly 136 estimated hours, with the longest chain running through Vault cleanup, Vault 2.0 and release. A slip in VC-002 or VR-002 pushes the mobile test and release.
triggers: A critical-path task exceeds its estimate.
New scope enters PHASE-3 or PHASE-5.
Device availability delays MT-002.
mitigation: PHASE-2 runs in parallel with the Vault branch.
Dependencies and critical path are stored as data and re-computed after change.
Phase gates require evidence, preventing hidden rework.
risks.contingency: Re-plan dates, surface the trade-off to the owner and cut optional scope before cutting verification.

controls.verification: Critical path recomputed from the DAG
Milestones and target dates updated after each gate

notes: R-001 is a hard policy control, not an ordinary technical risk: a violation blocks release.
Residual scores assume the listed controls are implemented and verified; an unimplemented control leaves the original score in force.
No risk is closed until its verification evidence is linked from execution/completed-tasks.json.
